sources.title: Azure Architecture Center: Publisher-Subscriber pattern
sources.supportRationale: Independent subscriptions and delivery/ordering considerations; concrete durability still follows the selected implementation.

sources.title: Azure Architecture Center: Competing Consumers pattern

sources.supportRationale: Fan-out exchange and separate subscriber queues; tutorial topology illustrates routing and is not claimed as a durable production configuration.

sources.title: Apache Kafka 4.1 Streams: Core concepts

sources.title: Google SRE: Handling overload
sources.supportRationale: Bounded work, resource/queue capacity and admission during sustained overload.

sources.title: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Transactional outbox

sources.title: RabbitMQ 4.1: Reliability guide

scenarios.theme: Risk and notifications share one queue and miss events. What changes?
scenarios.assumptions: Both applications require every eligible account fact, but their workers compete for one delivery stream. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Publish-Subscribe Pattern to shared role.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Risk and notifications share one queue and miss events. What changes?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Create independent application subscriptions under the selected broker, then let interchangeable workers share work within each application

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Separate subscriptions add retained state and monitoring

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: If only one of the applications should act on each task, competing delivery may have been the right contract; clarify the role first.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to pubsub, competing, rfanout; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: Risk is a day behind. Must notifications stop?
scenarios.assumptions: Risk is independently recoverable and notifications are required to remain available. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Publish-Subscribe Pattern to slow risk.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Risk is a day behind. Must notifications stop?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Isolate subscription progress/resources, bound risk backlog/retention and control its catch-up load while notifications continue under their own guarantee.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Storage/quotas cost resources and eventual retention exhaustion needs an explicit fallback

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Shared broker failure can still affect both; independent subscriptions are not unlimited physical isolation.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to pubsub, overload; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A new subscriber needs last month’s account history. Is subscribing enough?
scenarios.assumptions: The current channel promises only future publications and has no retained replay. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Publish-Subscribe Pattern to late subscription.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A new subscriber needs last month’s account history. Is subscribing enough?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Bootstrap from a supported authoritative snapshot/history with a defined handoff to live events, or choose retained history before promising completeness.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Bootstrap adds reconciliation and source load

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: An online-only listener can accept missing history, but that is a different product view.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to pubsub; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A new filter should include past premium accounts. What is missing?
scenarios.assumptions: Earlier events were excluded and the new consumer expects a complete derived view. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Publish-Subscribe Pattern to filter change.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A new filter should include past premium accounts. What is missing?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Determine whether historical replay exists and run an explicit bounded backfill/bootstrap with stable event/projection identity and a coordinated live catc

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Backfills consume capacity and may need a second view generation

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Merely editing the filter changes future eligibility, not necessarily already discarded history.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to pubsub, streams; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: An event secretly requires risk approval before billing success. What do you change?
scenarios.assumptions: The publisher claims final completion before the required subscriber has responded. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Publish-Subscribe Pattern to mandatory risk.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: An event secretly requires risk approval before billing success. What do you change?

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Model the mandatory approval as an explicit workflow/decision boundary with durable pending/final states and recovery ownership

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Explicit coordination adds latency/coupling, but the dependency already exists in business semantics

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Calling the message an event does not make the requirement optional.

scenarios.theme: A producer adds a field and one subscriber breaks. What now?
scenarios.assumptions: That subscriber uses a strict decoder while others accept the new payload. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Publish-Subscribe Pattern to schema reader.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A producer adds a field and one subscriber breaks. What now?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Check the actual schema/reader compatibility contract, deploy a compatible versioning transition and recover failed deliveries with stable identity after r

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Compatibility support and parallel versions add work

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Assuming every additive change is safe ignores real decoder behavior; dropping the subscriber silently may violate a required reaction.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to pubsub, rreliable; interview frequency is not claimed.
